channel.title: Crypto Daybook
channel.description: Crypto Daybook reports daily crypto news: market moves, Bitcoin and Ethereum updates, exchange and protocol developments, regulation and security incidents.

item.title: Checking a TRC-20 USDT Transfer on Tronscan
item.description: How to check a USDT transaction on Tronscan: search by hash or address, then confirm the status, genuine token contract, recipient and amount on Tron.

item.title: Base vs Solana When You’re Starting With Little Crypto
item.description: Base vs Solana for a beginner with low fees: both cost cents per transaction. Pick Base for Ethereum-style wallets, or Solana for lower, steadier fees.

item.title: Can smart contract wallets use cross chain bridges safely?
item.description: Smart contract wallets can send through most cross chain bridges, but the destination address must be controlled by a wallet deployed on the destination…

item.title: Who Can Call receiveMessage for a CCTP Mint?
item.description: The destinationCaller field names who may call receiveMessage for a CCTP mint. Set it to zero for open relaying or a bytes32 address for one caller.

item.title: Ethereum sets Dec. 15 test for Glamsterdam upgrade
item.description: Ethereum developers set Glamsterdam for Hoodi on Dec. 15, keeping a disputed storage-fee change that could force existing smart contracts to be fixed.

item.title: How to bridge USDC from Ethereum to Base as native USDC
item.description: How to bridge USDC from Ethereum to Base: use Circle CCTP to burn USDC on Ethereum and mint native USDC on Base, then check the token contract in your wallet.

item.title: Should You Delete Unused MetaMask Networks? Keep Funds Safe
item.description: Delete vs keep unused custom networks in MetaMask: remove one-off entries, keep networks you use or that hold funds, and restore balances with the same Chain ID.

item.title: Weekly vs monthly staking claims: monthly usually saves more
item.description: Claim staking rewards weekly or monthly? Monthly usually saves more on Ethereum mainnet because each claim has a fee, while weekly claims add extra gas costs.

item.title: What do I need before my first lending vault deposit? A checklist
item.description: Before your first lending vault deposit, have a backed-up wallet, the right asset and gas on its chain, and the vault address ready to deposit in one sitting.

item.title: Bridge fee or slippage? See where your ETH went
item.description: Received less ETH than sent after bridging? For ETH-to-ETH transfers, fees usually explain the gap: source gas and any bridge fee, not slippage.

item.title: Why a USDT Bridge Transfer Gets Stuck on Finality
item.description: Why is my USDT bridge transfer stuck? It is usually waiting for source finality or a relayer; check the bridge explorer to see whether to wait or claim.

item.title: SEC staff grants conditional relief for Molecule research tokens
item.description: SEC staff said it would not recommend enforcement over LabsCo’s proposed research tokens on stated terms, while stressing its response rests on those facts.

item.title: Injective’s Veyra upgrade adds tools for institutional asset trading
item.description: Injective’s Veyra upgrade went live at block 193,145,000, adding cross-chain transfers and quote-based trading tools for institutional tokenized assets.

item.title: New wallet vs protected RPC for MEV protection
item.description: Do I need a new wallet to use MEV protection? No. Keep your keys and add a protected RPC, or swap through an app with protection built in.

item.title: USDC vs USDC.e on Arbitrum: Pick the Right Token
item.description: USDC vs USDC.e difference on Arbitrum: USDC is issued by Circle; USDC.e is bridged from Ethereum. Learn to identify and convert each before sending.

item.title: Get BTC-backed tokens on Sui through Ethereum
item.description: To get Bitcoin onto the Sui network, buy WBTC or LBTC on Ethereum and bridge it to your Sui wallet with Suibridge; native BTC cannot move directly.

item.title: Supplying WBTC to Aave for variable interest
item.description: To supply wrapped bitcoin on Aave to earn interest, deposit WBTC into a market and receive aWBTC; the rate varies with borrowing demand and market capacity.

item.title: What happens if Bitcoin reorgs after a RenBridge transfer?
item.description: A blockchain reorg after a bridge transfer can delay a mint or leave bridged tokens without expected backing; the result depends on the bridge’s safeguards.

item.title: Gnosis Bridge contracts directly: an ERC-20 deposit
item.description: Learn how to use Gnosis Bridge contracts directly without the website: approve the Omnibridge mediator, call relayTokens, and track the ERC-20 on GnosisScan.

item.title: What Is Blockchain Finality, and Why Do Bridges Wait?
item.description: Transaction finality in blockchain marks when a transfer is settled: Bitcoin gains confidence with blocks, while Ethereum finalizes checkpoints in about 12.8 minutes.
